title: Segal fibers and cocartesian projection for interval strings
statement:
Let $\mathcal V$ be any monoidal infinity category in containing universes. Use $\mathcal M,q,p,r,r_\iota,K$ and the interval-string simplicial sets of [def-coef-enriched-interval-strings]. Then $\mathrm{Str}(\mathcal V)$ is a quasicategory, $p$ is a cocartesian fibration, and the consecutive-edge restriction functor is an equivalence
$$\mathrm{Str}(\mathcal V)_{[n]}\simeq\mathrm{Str}(\mathcal V)_{[1]}\times_{\mathcal V}\cdots\times_{\mathcal V}\mathrm{Str}(\mathcal V)_{[1]}$$
for every $n\geq0$, the $n=0$ expression being $\mathcal V$. The projection $r_\iota:\mathrm{Str}_\iota(\mathcal V)\to\Delta_K^{\mathrm{op}}$ is a cocartesian fibration. For a tuple $(M_0,\ldots,M_n)$ its fiber is naturally equivalent to
$$\prod_{i=1}^n (M_{i-1}\otimes -\downarrow M_i).$$
The factor is the degreewise pullback $\mathcal V\times_{\mathcal V,\mathrm{ev}_0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,\mathcal V)\times_{\mathcal V,\mathrm{ev}_1}\{M_i\}$, where the first map is $M_{i-1}\otimes-$; it denotes the coherent comma infinity category whose objects are $(V,f:M_{i-1}\otimes V\to M_i)$, with arrows and all higher simplices the commuting triangles and their coherent homotopies; the empty product is terminal. Under this equivalence consecutive-edge restriction is projection onto the corresponding factors. For an inert base map, cocartesian transport for $r_\iota$ restricts to its consecutive subinterval. An arrow over this restriction is $r_\iota$-cocartesian exactly when all its interval comparison arrows are equivalences; its image in $\mathrm{Str}(\mathcal V)$ is then $p$-cocartesian. These equivalences retain transformations, mapping spaces and all parameter simplices, and are natural in equivalences of endpoint objects and in restrictions to subintervals. No closedness or presentability is required.
